articles.title: Vizag woman visiting techie son in Melbourne dies after car crashes into Porsche; daughter-in-law killed
articles.summary: Vizag woman and her daughter-in-law died in a Melbourne Point Cook crash after their Toyota collided with a Porsche; Victoria Police investigating, GoFundMe launched.
articles.body: VISAKHAPATNAM: A visit to Australia turned into a tragedy for a Visakhapatnam family after a 33-year-old woman and her 67-year-old mother-in-law were killed when their car collided with a Porsche at a busy intersection in Point Cook, a south-western suburb of Melbourne, on Wednesday evening.The victims were identified as Neha, 33, and her mother-in-law Rama Devi, 67. Neha is survived by her husband and two children, both aged below 10 years.According to Visakhapatnam District Cricket Association (VDCA) member JKM Raju, Rama Devi was the wife of GT Prasad, a former treasurer and joint secretary of VDCA.Prasad, a former Hindustan Shipyard Limited (HSL) employee, and Rama Devi had travelled to Melbourne about two months ago to visit their son, who works as a software engineer there.Police said the Toyota Corolla carrying the two women collided with a Porsche Macan at the intersection of Boardwalk Boulevard and Saltwater Promenade in Point Cook. Both died at the scene despite emergency services’ efforts. Prasad’s daughter-in-law Neha was driving the car when the crash occurred. The 53-year-old Porsche driver survived and was taken to hospital with injuries.Victoria police have launched an investigation into the crash and are examining CCTV and other security footage captured shortly before the collision to establish the circumstances leading to the crash and determine whether speed was a factor.The tragedy has left the Telugu and Indian community in Melbourne shaken and plunged the victims’ family in Visakhapatnam into grief. articles.title: Offshore wind farms may be quietly stealing rain from Europe's coasts; study says: The more energy turbines pull from the wind, the less...
articles.summary: Tech News News: Europe is counting on offshore wind to move away from fossil fuels, and the North Sea is at the centre of that plan. The European Union wants 300 giga.
articles.body: Europe is counting on offshore wind to move away from fossil fuels, and the North Sea is at the centre of that plan. The European Union wants 300 gigawatts of offshore wind capacity by 2050. A new study from Germany suggests turbines at that scale could do more than generate electricity. They could also change where rain falls.Researchers at the Helmholtz-Zentrum Hereon found that very large offshore wind farm clusters may push more rain over the sea and leave parts of the coastline drier. In their simulations, coastal areas in Denmark, Germany, the Netherlands and the United Kingdom saw rainfall drop by up to 15%. The findings were published in the journal Communications Earth & Environment.Turbines slow the wind and stir up the air above the seaA wind turbine works by taking energy out of moving air. The wind behind it ends up slower and more turbulent.That turbulence mixes different layers of the atmosphere. Moist air gets pushed upward, where it cools, condenses and forms clouds. The result is more rain directly over the wind farms.The catch is that air can only carry so much moisture. When more of it falls over the sea, less is left by the time the air reaches land. Coastal regions downwind get less rain as a result.Ten years of weather data went into the North Sea rainfall modelThe team at Hereon's Institute of Coastal Systems - Analysis and Modeling used a high-resolution regional climate model called COSMO-CLM. The simulations ran on weather data from 2008 to 2017. Using a full decade smoothed out the effect of any single unusual year and gave a clearer view of long-term patterns.The model included existing wind farms and every zone marked for future development across the North Sea and the Baltic Sea."Our work helps ensure that the further expansion of offshore wind energy in Europe can be aligned with the requirements of climate protection, environmental protection and coastal management," said Dr Naveed Akhtar, the study's lead author.The study tested an extreme wind buildout, not Europe's actual planThe scenario was extreme by design. The researchers assumed maximum turbine deployment across all designated areas, which pushed installed capacity well past the 300 GW target. The goal was to make any climate effect large enough to detect and measure. It is not a forecast of what Europe will build.The results also describe long-term weather averages. They do not mean a specific town will miss rain on a specific day. Earlier Hereon research has shown that farm size, layout and turbine spacing affect how strongly turbines change the atmosphere, so a smaller or more spread-out buildout may have a milder effect.So will Europe's coasts lose rain? That depends on how the continent builds. The researchers are not arguing against offshore wind. They want more realistic scenarios tested for turbine density, farm size and placement, and they plan to study effects on the ocean and marine life next. For countries that share the same weather systems, where a wind farm goes may matter as much as how much power it produces.Get the latest technology news and updates. Download the TOI App.

articles.title: Newspaper headlines: 'Giddy King' and 'war of words' over Earl Spencer book
articles.summary: Most papers feature the latest from the royal feud on the second day of Diana's brother Earl Spencer's book being serialised in the Daily Mail.
articles.body:
Many of the front pages explore claims made by Earl Spencer in his book about his sister, Diana, Princess of Wales. The Daily Mail , which is serialising the book, says the late Queen offered to restore the princess's royal title on the day of her funeral.

It says Earl Spencer claims the news was conveyed to him by the Queen's private secretary and the-then Prince Charles, as they travelled to Diana's burial.

The Daily Express says a former aide to the King has said he told his staff never to criticise Diana, in order to preserve her memory.

The i Paper includes a column by the former BBC royal correspondent, Jennie Bond, who asks: "What is the point of reliving this agony?"

Similarly, the Sun 's front page headline asks "why is he doing this to the King now?" "Is it really to set the record straight", its editorial ponders, "or is it simply a money-spinning act of spiteful revenge?"

The royal editor of the Daily Mirror writes that the King, and Princes William and Harry will be "unanimous in their despair at this latest war of words".

Writing for the Guardian , Andy Burnham says Britain must fully commit to reaching net zero by 2050.

He says "British people are no longer insulated from the consequences of the climate crisis, and they do not want to be excluded from the solutions".

In its editorial, the Times says what it calls "zerophobia" will spread, unless the government makes the case for clean, homegrown energy which will be affordable, secure and an engine for growth.

The Telegraph reports that the chancellor is considering taxing holiday homes in the same way as second homes, rather than businesses, in the forthcoming budget -- adding thousands of pounds to the costs of running them. The paper says tourism bosses are warning that owners of holiday lets would be forced to sell up.

The Financial Times says Nick Candy, the Reform UK treasurer, met sanctioned officials from Nicaragua's regime before Metals Exploration - a firm in which he is the second-largest shareholder - won exploration rights in the country. Both Candy and the company say their actions complied with UK processes.

images.caption: Further allegations made in Earl Spencer's new book are in several of today's papers. The Daily Star headlines on King Charles being allegedly "giddily elated like a lottery winner" when he him called about Diana's death, her brother, Earl Spencer, claimed in the book. Buckingham Palace has strongly pushed back against the credibility of the book, saying: "His Majesty is mindful that the pain of fraternal grief can cloud reason, affect judgment and colour memory in ways others do not recognise, even many years after such a loss."

articles.title: Nova CNH: mudanças nas regras causaram prorrogação do vencimento | G1
articles.standfirst: Governo diz que novas regras exigem adaptações nos sistemas de trânsito para processar informações dos condutores. Medida é temporária e busca evitar prejuízos durante a transição.
articles.summary: Medida é necessária para adaptar sistemas e integrar a Senatran aos Detrans durante a implementação das mudanças.
articles.body:
Aplicativo da CNH do Brasil — Foto: Divulgação / Serpro

O Conselho Nacional de Trânsito (Contran) prorrogou a data de vencimento da Carteira Nacional de Habilitação (CNH) e da Autorização para Conduzir Ciclomotor (ACC) . Documentos com validade entre 5 de junho e 8 de dezembro passaram a ter uma nova data única de vencimento: 9 de dezembro .

Com a medida, o prazo foi ampliado em até 187 dias para as carteiras com vencimento a partir de 5 de junho.

Procurado pelo g1 , o Ministério dos Transportes afirmou que as mudanças aplicadas à emissão e à renovação da CNH justificam a prorrogação da validade dos documentos.

“O texto aprovado pelo Congresso Nacional trouxe alterações que exigem adequações operacionais e sistêmicas para a plena implementação das novas regras de renovação da CNH”, diz a pasta.

Segundo o ministério, uma dessas adequações é a “integração dos sistemas da Secretaria Nacional de Trânsito (Senatran) com os Departamentos Estaduais de Trânsito (Detrans)”.

Permitir a correta identificação da situação de cada condutor ;

Viabilizar o processamento das informações dos exames psicológico e de aptidão física e mental;

Garantir o registro dos resultados no prontuário do condutor .

“A medida é transitória e busca assegurar que o período necessário para a conclusão dessas adaptações não prejudique os condutores nem o exercício dos direitos previstos na nova legislação”, apontou a pasta.

Com a mudança, CNHs e ACCs vencidas desde junho voltam a ser consideradas válidas, e os motoristas não poderão ser punidos em fiscalizações por estarem com esses documentos vencidos.

Segundo o Contran, a prorrogação já está em vigor, e o condutor não precisa apresentar recurso caso o documento já esteja vencido. A medida, porém, não vale para motoristas com o direito de dirigir suspenso ou cassado.

Após a nova data de vencimento, os motoristas terão 30 dias para renovar os documentos.

articles.title: Unicamp 2027: veja principais novidades do vestibular | G1
articles.standfirst: Prova será realizada em 18 de outubro e terá 72 questões objetivas. Entre as novidades estão duas novas graduações, novos locais de prova e mudança na primeira chamada.
articles.summary: Prova será realizada em 18 de outubro e terá 72 questões objetivas. Entre as novidades estão duas novas graduações, novos locais de prova e mudança na primeira chamada.
articles.body:
Imagem aérea do campus da Unicamp em Campinas — Foto: Reprodução/EPTV

Falta exatamente um mês para a primeira fase do Vestibular 2027 da Unicamp . A prova será realizada no dia 18 de outubro , a partir das 9h, em um processo seletivo que oferece 2.523 vagas em 70 opções de cursos de graduação .

Nesta edição, a prova traz novidades para os candidatos que buscam uma oportunidade na instituição. O vestibular terá dois novos cursos, ampliação dos locais de aplicação das provas e uma alteração na convocação dos aprovados na primeira chamada. Veja a seguir .

A principal novidade desta edição é a criação de duas graduações no campus da Unicamp em Limeira (SP):

inteligência artificial e ciência de dados: 40 vagas, em período integral, oferecido conjuntamente pela Faculdade de Ciências Aplicadas (FCA) e pela Faculdade de Tecnologia (FT);

relações internacionais: 60 vagas, em período integral, oferecido pela FCA.

Com a criação de relações internacionais, o curso de administração no período noturno passa a oferecer 120 vagas, contra 180 anteriormente. A redução é compensada pelas 60 novas vagas da graduação.

Outra mudança em Limeira é a extinção do curso de tecnologia em saneamento ambiental a partir do Vestibular 2027. A medida não afeta os estudantes que já estão matriculados, que poderão concluir a formação.

A Unicamp também mudou a forma de convocação dos candidatos aprovados. Neste vestibular, a Comissão Permanente para os Vestibulares (Comvest) poderá convocar, na primeira chamada, mais candidatos do que o número de vagas disponíveis .

A estratégia, chamada de “overbooking”, considera o histórico de candidatos que são convocados, mas não efetivam a matrícula, principalmente por escolherem outras universidades. Segundo a Comvest, cerca de 40% dos candidatos convocados na primeira chamada não fazem a matrícula.

A mudança não significa aumento no número de vagas dos cursos . Caso a quantidade de candidatos que fizerem a pré-matrícula seja superior ao número de vagas, a universidade efetivará a matrícula dos candidatos mais bem classificados, respeitando o limite previsto.

Quem ficar fora do número de vagas poderá retornar à lista de classificados e ser convocado posteriormente, caso surjam vagas nas chamadas seguintes. Ao todo, estão previstas sete chamadas.

O Vestibular 2027 também terá novos locais de aplicação da primeira fase. Paulínia e Vinhedo foram incluídas entre as cidades que receberão a prova. Assim, o total em São Paulo passou para 33.

Na cidade de São Paulo, há outra novidade. Durante a inscrição, os candidatos puderam indicar a região da capital onde preferem fazer a prova. A escolha, porém, não garante um local específico.

A definição depende da disponibilidade de espaços e, caso a procura seja superior à capacidade, será considerada a ordem de efetivação das inscrições.

Na primeira fase, os candidatos terão entre duas e cinco horas para responder a 72 questões objetivas, cada uma valendo um ponto. A prova é dividida entre:

A segunda fase será realizada nos dias 29 e 30 de novembro , também a partir das 9h. A etapa é formada por questões dissertativas e uma redação.

No primeiro dia, todos os candidatos fazem a redação, a prova de língua portuguesa e questões interdisciplinares. No segundo, há questões interdisciplinares de ciências humanas e provas específicas de acordo com a área do curso escolhido.

Além das duas fases, alguns cursos exigem provas de habilidades específicas. Para música, os vídeos exigidos deveriam ser enviados pela internet entre 14 e 30 de setembro. Já para artes cênicas, artes visuais e dança, as provas específicas estão marcadas para os dias 2, 3 e 4 de dezembro.

Candidatos podem escolher até dois cursos

Entre os cursos com maior número de vagas estão o conjunto de opções do chamado curso 51, em período integral, com 170 vagas; Engenharia Mecânica, com 125; Administração noturno, com 120; Medicina, com 110; e Engenharia de Computação, com 90.

articles.title: Indígena de 106 anos comemora chegada de luz em aldeia em SC | G1
articles.standfirst: Aldeia Sol do Amanhecer, em Blumenau, agora tem luz. Indígenas do grupo Kaingang vivem no local.
articles.summary: Ela nunca havia morado em um local com luz elétrica antes.
articles.body:
Durante à noite, a escuridão tomava conta da aldeia indígena Sol do Amanhecer, localizada em Blumenau , no Vale do Itajaí, em Santa Catarina. O sol se punha e as crianças precisavam fazer o dever de casa à luz de velas e um fogo era aceso para todos pudessem se ver.

Tudo mudou com a instalação de um poste. Os sorrisos estamparam os rostos dos indígenas, que são do grupo Kaingang, após a conquista, que precisou tramitar na esfera judicial. "Povo está feliz", resumiu o cacique, Alcir Salvador.

Entre os moradores está Elena Cadete, que, aos 106 anos, pela primeira vez morou em um local com energia elétrica.

A luta para trazer a luz na aldeia começou há anos. Porém, foi em 2026 que o Departamento de Mediação e Conciliação de Conflitos Fundiários Indígenas do Ministério dos Povos Indígenas enviou um ofício à Defensoria Pública pedindo apoio.

Com esse suporte, a Defensoria entrou com uma ação civil pública. A aldeia fica no bairro Itoupava Norte, em uma área urbanizada.

A energia elétrica começou a funcionar no local em 5 de setembro.

Indígenas comemoram chegada da energia elétrica em aldeia de Blumenau, SC — Foto: Arquivo pessoal

Falta de iluminação atrapalhava rotina e gerava risco de acidentes

O cacique explicou que, antes da chegada da energia elétrica, a escuridão atrapalhava até os estudos dos filhos dele e ele acendia velas para que pudessem fazer os deveres de casa.

"Quando não tem vela, a gente tinha que fazer um fogareiro bem novamente, bem aceso, bem forte, para que eles pudessem fazer o 'tema' deles".

A faz de iluminação também era um risco para acidentes domésticos, principalmente no caso de Elena, e atrapalhava na hora da produção de artesanatos que são vendidos por eles.

Prejudicava também a própria convivência entre eles, que mal conseguiam ver uns aos outros à noite.

"Não foi fácil para conseguir essa claridade, para nós podermos nos enxergar, para nós podermos conversar".

Moradores com chaleira elétrica e Elene, em destaque — Foto: Arquivo pessoal

Conquista foi celebrada com chaleira elétrica

Com a ação civil pública em curso, as Centrais Elétricas de Santa Catarina (Celesc), companhia responsável pelo fornecimento de luz no estado, instalou um poste na aldeia.

A Defensoria Pública informou que vai encaminhar o processo à Justiça Federal, com o objetivo de ajudar a manter a energia elétrica no local de forma permanente.

Para comemorar a conquista, os moradores se juntaram para comprar uma chaleira elétrica.

O defensor público Jorge Calil Canut, que atuou no caso, destacou a celebração da chegada da luz na aldeia. "Uma chaleira elétrica é algo comum pra gente, mas pra eles significou muito. Algo simples e com custo muito baixo pode dar dignidade às pessoas", declarou.

articles.title: Infiltração no joelho: benefícios, riscos e limites do tratamento | G1
articles.standfirst: Corticoide, ácido hialurônico e PRP podem aliviar sintomas, mas não há comprovação de que esses recursos regenerem a cartilagem.
articles.summary: A infiltração no joelho com corticoide ou ácido hialurônico alivia a dor da artrose, mas não há provas de que esses recursos regenerem a cartilagem lesionada.
articles.body:
Infiltração no joelho não é solução para todos: entenda benefícios, limites e riscos — Foto: Adobe Stock

Danos às articulações tornam-se mais comuns com o envelhecimento, mas não preocupam apenas os idosos. Trauma, sobrecarga e processos degenerativos atingem diferentes idades e partes do corpo, mas em especial os joelhos, a maior articulação do corpo humano. Em 2019, 365 milhões de pessoas conviviam com a artrose no joelho, a articulação mais afetada pela doença , de acordo com a Organização Mundial da Saúde (OMS). Caminhar, levantar-se e subir escadas dependem dela. Preservar sua mobilidade significa um grande passo para manter a mobilidade e preservar autonomia.

Movidas pelo incômodo da dor, muitas pessoas esperam encontrar alívio em um procedimento simples. Essa expectativa não surge por acaso. Ela está associada à publicidade em torno das infiltrações veiculada nas redes sociais, em reportagens e em relatos de pacientes. O discurso destaca histórias de sucesso, novidades e produtos. Raramente, porém, contempla o fato de que essas terapias têm indicações específicas, podem ter resultados e duração variáveis.

Os procedimento passam a ser percebidos como uma tacada certa, de efeito completo e aplicável a qualquer joelho dolorido. Corticoide, ácido hialurônico, gel alemão, hidrogel, plasma rico em plaquetas (PRP), células-tronco, BMA e BMAC aparecem como alternativas para o mesmo problema. Não são. Começar pelo produto antes de compreender cada joelho é inverter o raciocínio.

Quantas pessoas você conhece que já fizeram diversos tratamentos e continuam com dor? Por que ela sempre volta? Um dos aspectos a serem considerados é o ponto de partida do tratamento. A pergunta a ser feita não é “qual é a melhor infiltração”, mas qual é o problema. Depois, é preciso definir o objetivo do tratamento e a evidência para as terapias a serem aplicadas em cada caso. Parece óbvio, mas nem sempre esse caminho prevalece.

Também é fundamental os pacientes saberem que há quatro objetivos possíveis para o tratamento: aliviar sintomas; modificar inflamação, líquido sinovial e sinalização biológica; reparar uma área lesada ou regenerar tecido próximo da cartilagem original. Um recurso pode aliviar a dor sem regenerar cartilagem. Isso não o torna um fracasso, apenas define o que se pode esperar dele. Tudo isso precisa estar bem pactuado e compreendido entre o médico e a pessoa à sua frente.

O médico explica benefícios, limites, riscos e duração do efeito. O paciente participa com seus sintomas, necessidades e possibilidades. Mais um aspecto a ser considerado é que medicamentos e procedimentos integram a estratégia de recuperação ou manutenção, mas não substituem sua base. Diretrizes internacionais mantêm no centro do cuidado com as articulações, em especial o joelho, medidas como a prática de exercício estruturado, o controle do peso quando necessário e o autocuidado. Músculos mais fortes e coordenados ajudam a distribuir e absorver cargas.

Entre adultos com sobrepeso ou obesidade e artrose, por exemplo, cada quilo perdido foi associado em pesquisas a cerca de quatro quilos a menos de carga sobre o joelho por passo. No ensaio clínico IDEA, dieta combinada a exercício promoveu perda média superior a 10% do peso em 18 meses e melhores resultados em parte dos desfechos que as intervenções isoladas. Essas medidas não produzem cartilagem nova, mas podem melhorar dor, função e autonomia.

Diante da massa de informações misturadas e veiculadas constantemente sobre infiltrações e outros tratamentos apresentados como promessas de melhora rápida, é importante entender o que cada recurso pode realmente oferecer. Corticoide, ácido hialurônico, hidrogéis, PRP e derivados da medula óssea têm composições, mecanismos, indicações e graus de evidência distintos. Não são versões concorrentes de uma mesma terapia. Alguns podem aliviar sintomas ou modificar o ambiente articular; outros são associados a promessas de reparação ou regeneração que ainda não foram comprovadas. Examinar cada um separadamente ajuda a ajustar expectativas e a avaliar com mais clareza seus possíveis benefícios, limites e riscos.

As aplicações de corticoide intra-articular reduz a inflamação e pode aliviar sintomas no curto prazo , mas não regenera cartilagem. Em um ensaio com 140 pacientes, o uso trimestral de triancinolona durante dois anos não foi melhor do que injeções de uma solução salina para controlar a dor. Ainda por cima, o uso da triancinolona se associou a uma perda maior de cartilagem. O resultado se refere àquele esquema de aplicações repetidas e não condena todo uso de corticoide. Mostra, porém, que indicação, frequência, duração do efeito e possíveis riscos precisam ser discutidos.

Outros nomes que aparecem com frequência são gel alemão, hidrogel e ácido hialurônico. Gel alemão é um apelido comercial, não uma categoria científica. Hidrogel, por sua vez, pode designar produtos com composições diferentes. Antes de compará-los ou atribuir benefícios a esses recursos, é necessário identificar a substância, a formulação e a indicação.

O ácido hialurônico está presente no líquido sinovial e participa de suas propriedades viscoelásticas. Algumas formulações podem aliviar a dor e melhorar a função, mas as recomendações divergem. Mais uma vez, alívio de sintomas não significa formação de cartilagem nova.

Em outro grupo estão os ortobiológicos, materiais derivados do próprio organismo usados para modificar o ambiente articular. O mais conhecido é o PRP, plasma obtido do sangue do paciente com maior concentração de plaquetas e de moléculas relacionadas à inflamação e ao reparo. Nem todo PRP, porém, é igual: o método de preparo, a concentração de plaquetas e a quantidade de leucócitos variam, produzindo materiais com características distintas.

Essa heterogeneidade ajuda a compreender por que os estudos chegam a resultados diferentes. No ensaio RESTORE, com 288 participantes, três aplicações de PRP não superaram as injeções de solução salina na redução da dor nem na preservação do volume da cartilagem após 12 meses.

Outras revisões encontraram resultados mais favoráveis ao PRP do que ao ácido hialurônico. Diferenças entre produtos, pacientes, métodos e desfechos avaliados ajudam a explicar a divergência. Nenhuma dessas evidências, no entanto, comprova ter ocorrido uma regeneração da cartilagem.

BMA e BMAC também são apresentados como ortobiológicos. BMA é o aspirado de medula óssea; BMAC, seu concentrado . Eles não correspondem a uma “seringa de células-tronco”, como às vezes são divulgados, mas a uma mistura de células sanguíneas, plaquetas, citocinas, fatores de crescimento e uma proporção muito pequena e variável de células progenitoras. Esses materiais podem modular o ambiente articular, mas não têm capacidade comprovada de regenerar a cartilagem.

As terapias celulares propriamente ditas, com células selecionadas, manipuladas ou expandidas em laboratório, pertencem a uma outra fronteira da ciência e continuam investigacionais. Uma revisão de 16 ensaios randomizados, com 807 participantes, concluiu que esses tratamentos provavelmente oferecem pouca ou nenhuma melhora clinicamente importante da dor e da função no período de três a seis meses. Também persistem incertezas sobre eventos adversos e resultados de longo prazo.

Como é possível perceber, o avanço no cuidado com os joelhos não está apenas em dispor de mais ferramentas, mas em distinguir aquilo que cada uma pode oferecer. Quando a publicidade e o produto ocupam o início da conversa, diagnóstico, exercício, educação, peso, sintomas e função passam para o segundo plano. Se o joelho volta ao centro, a ferramenta recupera seu lugar: não como promessa ou solução para todos, mas como parte de uma estratégia construída para cada paciente.

Os autores não prestam consultoria, trabalham, possuem ações ou recebem financiamento de qualquer empresa ou organização que se beneficiaria deste artigo e não revelaram qualquer vínculo relevante além de seus cargos acadêmicos.

articles.title: Suspeito de matar mulher em Curitiba estava foragido por violência doméstica havia três meses | G1
articles.standfirst: Joanderson Santos Silva foi a última pessoa vista com Maria Fernanda Naiser Fragais antes de ela ser encontrada morta com sinais de estrangulamento. Ele é procurado pela polícia.
articles.summary: Joanderson Santos Silva foi a última pessoa vista com Maria Fernanda Naiser Fragais antes de ela ser encontrada morta com sinais de estrangulamento. Ele é procurado pela polícia.
articles.body:
Joanderson Santos Silva, de 26 anos, suspeito de matar Maria Fernanda Naiser Fragais , de 43 anos, também é considerado foragido por ameaça, violação de domicílio e vias de fato em contexto de violência doméstica e familiar contra outra mulher.

O mandado de prisão preventiva contra o homem foi expedido em junho, três meses antes da morte de Maria Fernanda, encontrada morta dentro de uma vala no bairro Pinheirinho, em Curitiba , na terça-feira (15).

Ela foi vista pela última vez no domingo (13), ao sair de uma danceteria com o suspeito, e o corpo dela foi achado a cerca de 20 metros do estabelecimento, sem roupas e com sinais de estrangulamento.

Segundo a polícia, Joanderson foi identificado como a última pessoa que teve contato com Maria Fernanda.

A corporação divulgou imagens que mostram a vítima e Joanderson caminhando pela rua às 3h26. Oito minutos depois, às 3h34, o homem aparece sozinho, correndo de volta pelo caminho por onde os dois haviam passado. Assista ao vídeo acima.

A polícia divulgou uma foto de Joanderson Santos Silva e pediu ajuda da população para localizá-lo.

Informações que possam ajudar a polícia a encontrar o investigado podem ser repassadas de forma anônima pelo telefone 197, da PCPR, ou pelo 0800-643-1121, diretamente à equipe de investigação.

Joanderson Santos Silva, de 26 anos, é o principal suspeito da morte dela e está foragido. — Foto: PCPR

Vítima estava visitando familiares que não via há 14 anos

Maria Fernanda morava em Palmas, no Sul do Paraná, e saiu da cidade na segunda-feira (7) com destino a Curitiba. Segundo a filha, Eduarda Naiser, ela não via os familiares que moram na capital há 14 anos.

Na noite de sábado (12), Maria Fernanda foi a uma danceteria no bairro Pinheirinho, acompanhada de uma sobrinha. Durante a festa, ela conheceu Joanderson Santos Silva. Os dois permaneceram juntos ao longo da noite.

Segundo o responsável pelo estabelecimento, as câmeras mostram o homem chegando ao local, comprando uma bebida e, depois, Maria Fernanda entrando. Os dois aparecem bebendo e fumando juntos antes de deixarem a danceteria.

O proprietário afirmou à RPC, afiliada da TV Globo no Paraná, que não houve registro de agressões dentro do estabelecimento e que os dois saíram juntos e aparentavam estar bem.

A sobrinha percebeu que Maria Fernanda havia desaparecido e saiu para procurá-la, mas não conseguiu encontrá-la. A família comunicou o desaparecimento à polícia no domingo (13).

Na terça-feira (15), o corpo da mulher foi encontrado dentro de uma vala na Rua Gertrúdes Cruz de Andrade, a cerca de 20 metros da danceteria, sem roupas e com sinais de estrangulamento.

articles.title: Not just 'Nice Guy Eddie': Lib Dems eager for leader to show radical side at party conference
articles.summary: There is a sizeable group of Lib Dem MPs who openly question whether the party's problem is with its leader, while others support his stance.
articles.body:
Discontent bubbles not far from the surface as the Liberal Democrats gather for their conference this weekend.

Two years on from their best ever general election result, conversations with those on the party's frontbench, its MPs, and backroom staff reveal a frustration at what many see as a failure to capitalise on that success.

Polling by YouGov in the build up to the conference highlighted the Lib Dems "have seen no real growth in support since the last general election" and if anything have slipped back.

"We lack the ability to say something new or interesting," said one senior Lib Dem MP.

A frontbencher said: "With the possible exception of our position on Trump, you could characterise most of our press lines as 'a Lib Dem spokesperson said, steady on now, gently does it'."

Others describe the party's approach as "boring" and are spooked by the rise of the Green Party under Zack Polanski.

The party's leadership are aware of the anger. They insist this conference will be a "gear shift".

Daisy Cooper, the deputy leader, told me it would be "a gloves-off kind of conference".

"You'll see a bit of fighting talk," she said.

Some of the caution until now has been deliberate. The party's leadership met over the last few months and discussed whether to copy Polanski's punchy, social media-focused style but decided it wouldn't appeal to the well-heeled areas of southern England that form the Lib Dem heartlands.

But at all levels of the party there is an acknowledgement they lag behind other parties on grabbing attention on social media, highlighted by Andy Burnham's "social first" approach.

The party has only recently rolled out training for its MPs on making social videos, something senior figures despair at.

"When we have a success we're very good at getting a leaflet sent out to supporters straight away," one senior MP said. "But we don't do that for socials."

Digital and social media will be a focus of at least 17 fringe events at conference, as the party tries to improve its online communications.

But others worry that social media is just the medium and the problem is with the message.

One MP raised the majority of voters (52% according to YouGov,) who view the party as "weak" in recent polling; and the tendency to say it's unclear what the party stands for (43% believing the party was weak, to 18% thinking it was strong).

"We need to become bolder and more radical," a senior MP added. "We need to be angry on behalf of our constituents."

Another Lib Dem MP said: "We are stuck fighting the guerilla politics of local campaigning. There is no broader articulation of what a vision for Liberal Britain is."

Even those most loyal to Davey admit the party was struggling to offer a clear and coherent message. The Lib Dems' success at the last general election was, the party's own strategists believe, because voters wanted to remove the Conservatives and the Lib Dems benefitted from that anti-Tory sentiment.

"We haven't yet answered why people should vote for us rather than against the Tories," admitted one senior advisor.

In public, Lib Dem MPs are often coy about the possibility of a coalition government with Labour after the election. In private, there are no such reservations.

In an election many think could produce a hung parliament with no party in overall majority, the Lib Dem ambition is to be kingmakers to block a Reform government.

"If you're a serious political party you exist to be in government," the same senior adviser said.

Lib Dem strategists are confident they can retain most of the 72 seats they won in 2024. Their sights now are on the 27 others where they came second, most of which were won by the Conservatives.

The party's leadership characterise the last two years since the general election as "stage one" when a largely new intake of MPs bedded into their constituencies.

"Stage two is winning the air war and describing exactly what Liberal Britain looks like. You'll see a lot of that at conference," said Cooper.

Of her boss, party leader Sir Ed, she said: "He's not just nice guy Eddie. I think you're going to see him being a bit more gritty because he's a real fighter."

She added Davey saw the battle with Reform UK as the "fight of our lives".

Critics within the party point out that promise of fighting talk to take on Reform UK accompanied the last Lib Dem conference . Yet little has changed in the party's national standings.

Join EU migration pact to tackle small boats, says Ed Davey

Change voting system before next election, Davey urges Burnham

Lib Dems offer alternative to extremes of Reform and Greens, Davey says

There is a sizeable group of Lib Dem MPs, and members of its frontbench, who openly question whether their problem is not with the message, nor the strategy, but with Davey, the leader.

"I think he's holding us back," said one of the party's spokespeople who is planning a tilt at the leadership if a race is triggered.

"The atmosphere is ripe for a leadership challenge," another MP, talking of the frustrations in the party, said.

"But we don't have a Wes Streeting," they added, referring to Labour's defence secretary whose challenge to Sir Keir Starmer undermined his leadership.

"There is a lack of an ambitious, young alternative putting themselves out there to show a different way."

Davey's supporters in the party point to his experience of government and insist there is no one better to replace him. They also dismiss national polling as the way to measure the Lib Dem's standing.

"I'd like to be on more than 10% [in national opinion polls]," one frontbencher loyal to Davey said. "But I'd prefer to be on 10% and looking at winning 80 seats than on 15% and winning four."

"You look at our ground game and you look at our local election results," another said, pointing to gains the party made at this year's May elections. "That shows you that our strategy is definitely working."

But frustration bubbles away. And plenty in the party are looking at alternatives to Davey, like the party's President Josh Babarinde or Cooper, and question why they aren't setting out alternative visions.

Both will give speeches at the conference, as will the home affairs spokesperson Max Wilkinson.

So what of Cooper, who many consider the frontrunner to succeed Davey?

"Ed is absolutely the right leader," she tells me. "I really like being deputy leader to Ed. We work together as a team. I think we complement each other."

Would she want to be leader? "There is no vacancy," she says.

Ever? "There is no vacancy at the moment," she replies.

articles.title: ICE deports ex-Liberian fighter accused of torture, recruiting child soldiers
articles.summary: ICE removed Amos Sheik Massaquoi from the United States to Liberia over alleged killings, torture and child soldier recruitment during the civil wars.
articles.body: EXCLUSIVE — A former Liberian combatant believed to have ordered and participated in killings, torture and the recruitment of child soldiers was deported after spending nearly two decades in the United States. U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement removed Amos Sheik Massaquoi, 55, to Liberia on Aug. 11, officials told Fox News Digital. He is believed to have served as chief bodyguard to Maj. Gen. Daniel Chea, a former leader in Charles Taylor's National Patriotic Front of Liberia. ICE said Massaquoi is believed to have ordered and participated in extrajudicial killings, acts of torture, arbitrary arrests and detentions, forced labor and the recruitment of child soldiers during the Liberia's civil wars, from 1989 to 2003. "If you are a confirmed human rights violator, and you believe you can hide in the United States, you are mistaken," ICE Chicago Field Office Director Frank Padula said. LIBERIA AGREES TO ACCEPT 1,200 THIRD-COUNTRY DEPORTEES FROM US WITHIN A YEAR "ICE will pursue, arrest and remove any individuals who committed atrocities abroad and ensure our communities are not used as a sanctuary from accountability." EXCLUSIVE: 25 YEARS AFTER 9/11, ICE SAYS MORE THAN 2K KNOWN OR SUSPECTED TERRORISTS HAVE BEEN DEPORTED Massaquoi legally entered the U.S. in August 2006 but was only authorized to remain until Nov. 6 of that year, according to ICE. He remained in the country until Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) arrested him in Maryland in August 2019 for being illegally present in the U.S. An immigration judge granted him bond less than two months later, and he was released. TRUMP DOJ ESCALATES CITIZENSHIP CRACKDOWN ON GROUP ACCUSED OF HIDING TERROR TIES, VIOLENT CRIMES Massaquoi was taken back into custody by ICE Baltimore April 1, 2025, after officials said he failed to comply with the terms of his release. An immigration judge ordered him removed the following month. ICE said Massaquoi also received specialized military training at an academy in China in 2004, one year after Liberia's second civil war ended. Liberia's civil wars killed almost 250,000 people, most of them civilians, according to the United Nations. Taylor, who led the rebel movement before becoming Liberia's president, was later convicted of aiding and abetting crimes committed by rebel forces in neighboring Sierra Leone. He was sentenced to 50 years in prison, according to the Residual Special Court for Sierra Leone. FORMER SYRIAN PRESIDENT ASSAD SENTENCED TO DEATH IN ABSENTIA "Amos Sheik Massaquoi is believed to have engaged in cruelty and terror, marked by killings, torture, forced labor, unlawful imprisonment and the recruitment of children into armed conflict," HSI Maryland Special Agent in Charge Akil Baldwin said. "If it is confirmed that an individual has engaged in such bloodshed anywhere in the world, then you have no place in the United States." articles.title: Judge orders Trump to give 30 days' notice before any 'demolition' at Kennedy Center
articles.summary: The order comes after Trump was photographed onboard Air Force One looking at a poster that appeared to tout the demolition of the site.
articles.body:
A US federal judge has ruled the Trump administration must give 30 days' notice before any "demolition" occurs to the Kennedy Center, as President Donald Trump warned the Washington DC performing arts venue could be "ripped down".

The order comes after Trump was photographed onboard Air Force One looking at a poster with a headline that appeared to tout the demolition of the site.

US District Judge Christopher Cooper ordered a detailed report of the centre's "temporary closure" for emergency repairs, and for written notice of any change to the scope of the project.

In May, Cooper ordered the removal of Trump's name from the building.

In a document filed to court on Thursday before the judge's ruling, Kennedy Center executive director Matt Floca said the temporary closure was to repair safety hazards and would last seven days "unless extended".

On Tuesday, the Kennedy Center's board of trustees voted - for the third time since February - to close the venue down for two years.

Trump then took to Truth Social to write that the board, which is chaired by him and includes his cabinet members and allies, voted "almost unanimously" to close the venue "for safety reasons".

He has argued that the venue is badly in need of repair, and that by adding his name to the building it will be able to secure renovation funding.

"I think that the Trump administration should certainly have recognition because, frankly, if we don't do that, it's going to close," he told reporters in Charlotte, North Carolina, on Wednesday. "It'll end up being ripped down."

On Wednesday, Trump was photographed through a window of Air Force One looking at a placard that appeared to read: "Kennedy Center DEMOLISHED."

On Thursday, Cooper ordered the Trump administration to provide at least 30 days' notice ahead of any change in construction plans.

That order came after congresswoman Joyce Beatty, an ex officio Kennedy Center board member, asked the judge to make "crystal clear that its order prohibits demolishing the structure".

Beatty, a Democrat, had previously sued to halt changes to the Kennedy Center, and to strip Trump's name from the building.

Congress established the centre as a memorial to President John F Kennedy, who was assassinated in 1963.

Some critics argue that congressional action is required to make changes to the building, and that the need for renovations is exaggerated.

articles.title: University event with Hasan Piker in Texas draws backlash from both sides of the aisle
articles.summary: Hasan Piker's planned UT Austin event drew bipartisan backlash from Ted Cruz, Greg Abbott and Henry Cuellar over his past remarks on 9/11 and Hamas.
articles.body: The University Democrats, a student group at the University of Texas at Austin, unintentionally brought together political heavyweights from both sides of the aisle after announcing earlier this month an event featuring controversial Twitch streamer Hasan Piker. Piker, who hosts hours-long streams on a daily basis, is known for his incendiary rhetoric, anti-capitalist views and anti-Israel stance. The streamer has recently become a source of an offline debate over how Democrats engage with voters. According to University Democrats, Piker is expected to address "a variety of topics, ranging from immigration, to genocide, to the future of the Democratic Party." The group noted that the event, scheduled for Sept. 30 and limited to UT Austin students, staff and faculty, will include a Q&A session. WHO IS HASAN PIKER? MEET THE FAR-LEFT STREAMER WHO IS STIRRING UP CONTROVERSY AND DIVIDING DEMOCRATS On Monday, University Democrats claimed in an X post that UT Austin was violating its own policies by "failing to accommodate" the event and provide a large venue. Fox News Digital was not able to independently verify the club's claim. It didn't take long for Texas lawmakers from both sides of the aisle, including Gov. Greg Abbott, Sen. Ted Cruz and Rep. Henry Cuellar, to voice their disapproval of the event and condemn Piker. "Hasan Piker’s scheduled appearance at the University of Texas is deeply concerning," Cuellar wrote on X. "Free speech allows difficult and controversial views, but it does not require anyone to stay silent when someone has a history of hateful comments about Jewish Americans, 9/11, and Hamas terrorism. "Jewish students at UT should not be made to feel targeted or unsafe on their own campus." PIKER DEMANDS DEMOCRATS DEFEND HIM FROM ATTACKS, CLAIMS HE’S NO ‘TOXIC RADICAL FORCE' In a statement provided to Fox News Digital, Cruz said Piker's appearance at an event hosted by University Democrats was a statement about the status of the Democratic Party. "Hasan Piker is an America-hating Marxist who has said that America deserved 9/11 and celebrates political violence against Republicans," Cruz's statement said. "Americans are entitled to free speech, but it is incumbent upon good people to condemn Piker's incitement. Instead, some Democrats are bringing him to college campuses, while almost all other Democrats are conspicuously silent or worse. It says everything about the state of their party." Andrew Mahaleris, press secretary for Texas Gov. Greg Abbott, also chimed in, telling Jewish News Syndicate (JNS), "Terrorist sympathizers have no place in Texas." "Hasan Piker said America deserved 9/11 and praised the brutal terrorist organization Hamas. University Democrats at UT Austin are choosing to amplify that disgusting rhetoric," Mahaleris told JNS. CONTROVERSIAL STREAMER HASAN PIKER'S LECTURE AXED BY UNIVERSITY OF WASHINGTON AMID FREE SPEECH QUESTIONS While lawmakers focused their criticism on Piker's past rhetoric, the streamer pushed back, saying the pressure campaign to cancel the event presented a constitutional issue. "Ted cruz, greg abbott ken paxton and now, henry cuellar have demanded that i have my speech at UT austin get cancelled. it's a public university. this is a direct violation of the 1st amendment. free speech must be protected. dems should push back against this attack!," Piker wrote on X. The controversy over the event reflects growing tension over Piker's increasing prominence on the political stage. While some argue that he brings in younger voters, critics say his rhetoric goes too far. articles.title: Tunisia floods disrupt capital as heavy rain traps motorists and residents
articles.summary: Recurring floods disrupt daily life in Tunis, raising questions about drainage, transport and flood preparedness.
articles.body:
Tunis, Tunisia – Heavy rain brought parts of Tunisia’s capital to a standstill on Thursday, flooding roads and homes, trapping people in cars and disrupting electricity and internet services.

Home to nearly three million people, the Greater Tunis region has faced repeated flooding in recent years. Thursday’s flooding came only months after severe January rains caused widespread disruption across the capital and other parts of the country, leaving several people dead and causing significant damage.

Weather warnings had been issued in advance, but the decision to suspend classes in Tunis was announced only shortly before it took effect. Parents rushed to schools to collect their children as the rain intensified and traffic backed up across the capital.

Videos shared online showed flooded streets, cars stranded in rising water and what appeared to be power lines catching fire. Residents also reported power and internet cuts and water entering homes.

Fatma, a 35-year-old employee in Tunis, said the situation deteriorated quickly as she struggled to get home safely.

“At about 4pm, the road became almost unrecognisable. The tunnel leading to Bab Saadoun was completely closed because of the rain,” she told Al Jazeera.

“Most people were stranded by the roadside for hours, waiting for public transport that never came. I saw three cars that filled with water and broke down, and people carrying their children on their shoulders.”

“Every season, the same thing happens. Roads close and traffic comes to a complete standstill. All the drains start overflowing with waste,” she said.

The National Institute of Meteorology had warned of locally heavy thunderstorms on Thursday, including heavy rain over short periods that could cause flooding, disrupt traffic and overwhelm drainage networks. It also warned of potential power cuts.

“Tunisia has become used to these disasters. Every year, we end up flooded even when there is little rain,” said Intissar, 33, from the Lafayette area of Tunis.

She blamed local authorities for failing to carry out preventive work before the rainy season.

“This is work that should have been done during the summer,” she said.

But she also acknowledged the role of residents.

“We cannot deny the responsibility of citizens who dump waste that blocks drainage channels,” she said.

At a government meeting in August, officials called for drainage networks and waterways to be cleaned and flood-protection work to be accelerated. The government said 29 flood-protection projects were under way across the country.

The flooding comes as Tunisia prepares for a national march in Tunis on Saturday, with organisers calling for the release of four activists detained in connection with the Al-Soumoud Flotilla. The march is scheduled for 5pm, as rain is forecast to continue through Saturday.

Fatma said the lack of reliable public transport, combined with repeated flooding, was making it increasingly difficult for people to manage without cars.

“The problem makes people look for their own solutions. That is why most people are trying to find a way to buy a car, because it has become difficult to live without one with these recurring problems,” she said.

The flooding also came as students returned to schools and universities this week, adding pressure to roads and public transport.

For Fatma, the disruption is becoming a familiar pattern.

“This shows that the state has no vision. It is caught off-guard just like citizens are,” she said.

articles.title: F-16 fighter jet crashes in residential area in northern Michigan
articles.summary: The pilot safely ejected from the Texas Air National Guard jet in Grand Traverse County, and no injuries were reported on the ground.
articles.body: A U.S. F-16 fighter jet pilot safely ejected before the aircraft crashed in northern Michigan on Thursday afternoon, officials said. The incident occurred in Grand Traverse County when the jet “experienced an incident” during a routine training mission, a spokesperson for the Texas Military Department said. Michael Kroll, spokesperson for the Michigan Department of Military and Veterans Affairs, confirmed the jet was an F-16 from the Texas Air National Guard. The pilot is stable and was transferred to a local hospital, Michigan State Police said. The training mission originated out of the Air National Guard’s Combat Readiness Training Center in Alpena, Michigan, the military department said. There have been no reports of civilian injuries in the incident, which occurred in a residential area, Blair Township Supervisor Nicole Blonshine said in a phone interview Thursday afternoon. Blonshine said she did not witness the crash but heard it from her office. A witness, Nicole Conrad, said her kids noticed the military jet first. “I hear a big boom, and then I see a colorful parachute and this guy floating down from the sky,” she told NBC News. Ed Wilson, another witness, said he saw the plane going down, followed by an explosion and black smoke. “The jet just went straight in with a nose up and disappeared,” he said. Social media video verified by NBC News appears to show a column of black smoke rising near a home in the area of the reported crash. A hazardous chemical spill related to the crash led to an evacuation of all business and residential properties within a 1-mile radius, state police said. The order was lifted as of 9:44 p.m. Air traffic control audio obtained by NBC News describes the declaration of a possible mayday after the plane “may have taken a bird.” It goes on to describe “a lot of black smoke” after it reported “it appears that they may have lost an engine and ejected.” The Texas Military Department spokesperson said the incident is under investigation. An F-16 Fighting Falcon is a “compact, multi-role fighter aircraft” that is “highly maneuverable and has proven itself in air-to-air combat and air-to-surface attack,” according to the Air Force.

articles.title: Former Assad officer sentenced to 60 years in US for torture
articles.summary: Former Syrian official sentenced to 60 years in US prison for torturing prisoners under al-Assad’s regime.
articles.body:
A former Syrian military official convicted of torturing prisoners during the rule of former President Bashar al-Assad has been sentenced to 60 years in a United States prison.

A federal judge in Los Angeles sentenced Samir Ousman Alsheikh on Thursday. A jury found him guilty in March of one count of conspiracy to commit torture and three counts of torture while in charge of Syria ‘s infamous Adra Prison from roughly 2005 to 2008.

“The conduct was heinous, unimaginably cruel, and almost unspeakably violent and brutal,” the judge said before announcing the sentence.

Human rights groups and the United Nations have accused the Syrian government officials of widespread abuses in detention facilities, including torture and arbitrary detention of thousands of people, in many cases without informing their families.

US prosecutors said Alsheikh, seeking to quash political dissent, sent certain prisoners to a wing of Adra where they were held in small isolation cells and tortured.

At the two-week trial, three victims recounted beatings while suspended from pipes on the ceiling for hours or days and the use of a device that folded their bodies in half at the waist, according to a press release from the US Department of Justice. One person testified that Alsheikh stomped on the device with his foot, according to the department.

“Defendant knew that what he was doing was wrong,” Justice Department prosecutors said in a sentencing memo filed this month. “Nonetheless, he ordered and participated in the torture of his victims because he had the power to do so and because he thought he would never be held accountable.”

The memo included statements from several victims, one of whom, Nidal Shikhani, said he can “still hear the screams of others begging for mercy, repeating, ‘Leave me, leave me.’”

The prosecutors asked US District Judge Hernan D Vera for a minimum sentence of 80 years. Alsheikh’s lawyers, Nina Marino and Collin Cate, called for a five-year sentence, noting that he is 74 years old and has “significant medical and cognitive conditions”. They also said he was willing to be deported to Syria, where a new government has sought to hold Assad-era security officials accountable.

“Whatever moral weight this case carries in the broader arc of history — however much the world, or the victims, or the public might wish the sentence to ‘send a message’ — that desire cannot be the foundation of a just sentence,” Marino and Cate wrote in their September 3 memo.

Alsheikh came to the US in 2020 and applied for citizenship, but the Justice Department said he lied about his past. Federal authorities arrested him at Los Angeles international airport in July 2024.

Jurors also convicted him in March of lying to US immigration authorities and fraudulently obtaining a green card and attempting to naturalise as a US citizen.

“The acts Alsheikh ordered and directly participated in are gruesome and disturbing. We would like to offer our gratitude to the brave victims who testified leading to today’s sentencing,” Heith Janke, assistant director of the FBI’s criminal division, said in a press release Thursday.

Al-Assad was ousted in a lightning rebel offensive in December 2024, bringing a 14-year civil war to an end, but the country has continued to suffer from sporadic outbreaks of violence.

In March 2025, armed groups aligned with al-Assad ambushed the new government’s security forces on Syria’s coast. A government counteroffensive then spiralled into sectarian revenge attacks and the massacre of hundreds of civilians from the Alawite religious minority, to which al-Assad belongs.

On Thursday, three people were sentenced in the Syrian city of Aleppo in connection with the violence. One member of the pro-Assad groups was sentenced to death and another to life in prison, while a member of the government security forces who took part in the revenge attacks was convicted of murder and sentenced to 20 years in prison.

articles.title: Juror who blocked Lindsay Clancy verdict disputes fellow jurors' claims: report
articles.summary: Michael Desronvil, the holdout Lindsay Clancy juror, disputes fellow jurors' claims he expressed doubts about the prosecution's case during deliberations.
articles.body: The lone holdout juror whose refusal to find Lindsay Clancy not guilty by reason of insanity led to a mistrial is speaking publicly for the first time, disputing claims from fellow jurors that he expressed doubts about the prosecution's case. Michael P. Desronvil said in a statement to NewsNation that he never wavered in his belief prosecutors proved Clancy knew what she was doing when she strangled her three young children in January 2023. "I didn't have any doubts. As I tried to explain different possible theories during deliberation, I kept getting cut off as if I had doubts based on the evidence present," Desronvil said. LINDSAY CLANCY HOLDOUT JUROR ‘LOOKED AT THE CASE AND HE MADE THE CALL,’ HIS BROTHER SAYS "Based on all the physical evidence, key witnesses and what the prosecution presents, I thought it was enough proof that she knew exactly what she was doing and planned." His comments directly contradict accounts from fellow jurors, who said after the mistrial that Desronvil appeared to acknowledge reasonable doubt during deliberations but still refused to join the other 11 jurors in finding Clancy not guilty by reason of insanity. The jury deadlocked 11-1, with Desronvil standing alone in favor of convicting Clancy rather than accepting her insanity defense, prompting Judge William Sullivan to declare a mistrial. JUROR ON LINDSAY CLANCY TRIAL SAYS 'WE LET DOWN LINDSAY' FOLLOWING MISTRIAL The public statement comes as Plymouth County prosecutors weigh whether to retry Clancy, whose attorneys have also floated the possibility of resolving the case without another jury trial. Fox News contributor Jonathan Turley previously told Fox News Digital that prosecutors face the difficult task of deciding whether they can persuade a future jury to unanimously reject Clancy's insanity defense after the first panel failed to reach a verdict. "The question is whether they could ever get a jury, particularly in Massachusetts, that would unanimously vote against this defendant," Turley said. "For prosecutors, they have to weigh that, but they may find the alternative equally unappealing — to simply walk away and say, 'There are three dead children here, but we just don't think we could ever win this case.'" Clancy, a former labor and delivery nurse, admitted killing her children — Cora, 5, Dawson, 3, and Callan, 8 months — but argued she was not criminally responsible because she was suffering from severe mental illness at the time of the killings. Prosecutors argued she planned the murders and understood the wrongfulness of her actions. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Judge Sullivan has ordered jurors' identities and questionnaires sealed, citing safety concerns following the high-profile mistrial. Clancy is due back in court Sept. 29 as prosecutors determine whether to seek a retrial.

articles.title: Syria warns Israel poses ‘the greatest threat’ to Middle East stability
articles.summary: UNSC meeting on Syria turned into a heated debate between Israel and Turkiye over troops in Syrian territory.
articles.body:
The United Nations Security Council’s monthly meeting on Syria’s post-Assad transition has seen Syria, Israel and Turkiye trade accusations over who can rightfully have a military presence on Syrian soil.

Syria’s Permanent Representative to the UN, Ibrahim Olabi, told council members on Thursday that he had hoped to focus on the country’s progress but was compelled to address Israel’s actions in Syria, according to a UN summary of the meeting.

“Israel penetrated our villages, displaced our people, bombed our facilities while we chose to spare the region further suffering,” he said, accusing Israel of responding to mediation efforts and dialogue with “air strikes, incursions and violations”.

Olabi said Israeli aggression poses “the greatest threat facing the stability of the entire region, not just Syria”, pointing to an emergency declaration by 44 nations outside the council chamber that condemned a visit by Israeli leadership to Jabal al-Sheikh inside Syrian territory on September 9 as an unlawful act and a “blatant violation” of international law.

Israeli Ambassador to the UN Danny Danon downplayed Israel’s presence in Syria and shifted the focus to Turkiye.

He warned that Ankara planned to expand its military capabilities inside Syria and take over the country, the UN report said.

“If Israel’s tiny defensive buffer is considered a threat to Syrian stability, then what about a foreign power that controls a much larger portion of Syrian territory and is building its military presence there? I am talking about Turkiye,” he said.

“Turkiye has 20,000 troops and over 100 bases in Syria, controlling 5 percent of its territory, 50 times larger than Israel’s ‘security buffer’. Turkiye is now following the Iranian proxy playbook.”

Turkish Ambassador to the UN Ahmet Yildiz said Turkish forces based in Syria were there at the invitation of Damascus.

“We categorically reject Israel’s attempts to smear Turkiye’s legitimate cooperation with Syria and portray it as a threat in an effort to justify its own violations of international law,” he said.

He accused Israel of undermining this trajectory through “reckless attacks” and incursions into Syrian territory, and called on Israel to de-escalate and withdraw its forces.

Syria’s ambassador denounced the debate.

“Syria’s meetings should not be talking about proxy issues any more. That was the case during the regime era. It should no longer be the case. It’s frankly traumatising,” he said.

articles.title: Ohio mother of 16 kids found living in squalid home pleads not guilty to endangering her children
articles.summary: Elizabeth Siders, 34, also pleaded not guilty to charges of sexual battery and unlawful sexual conduct with a minor in a separate case.
articles.body: The mother of 16 children found living in squalid conditions in an Ohio house has pleaded not guilty to endangering her children, as well as sexual battery of a minor in a separate case. Elizabeth Siders, 34, appeared in Vinton County court Wednesday for her arraignment. She was arrested June 30 along with her husband, Gary Siders Jr., and her in-laws Gary Siders Sr. and Christina Siders. Elizabeth Siders pleaded not guilty to 19 counts of child endangerment in the case related to her children. Prosecutors said that the children were found in horrific conditions, in a home littered with feces, and that some of the children were unable to speak. She also pleaded not guilty to two charges each of sexual battery and unlawful sexual conduct with a minor in a separate case. NBC News has reached out to her attorney for comment. Siders and her husband were indicted Aug. 21 in the sexual battery case. The indictments accuse Gary Siders Jr., 36, and Elizabeth Siders of sexual abuse against a minor, who was between the ages of 13 and 16 in 2022. The indictments indicate the victim was not one of Elizabeth Siders’ children, but they describe her as acting “in loco parentis,” meaning she was responsible for the victim’s care. She hung her head in court when a judge ordered her Wednesday to have no contact with her children, the minor victim or her husband. The judge set her bond at $250,000, on top of her $300,000 child endangerment bond. She remained in jail Thursday. Her defense attorney, Thomas Stolly, told the judge she misses her children and questioned whether she herself is a victim. “We have an individual in Elizabeth who was married at age 15, who has essentially been pregnant for the better part of two decades, who has never fully gone through any postpartum period,” Stolly said, according to NBC affiliate WSAZ of Huntington, West Virginia. He said he was concerned about the effects she may suffer given the repeated births and a lack of regular medical care. The Siders children, ages 1½ to 18, are in state custody. Stolly previously asked for a competency evaluation for Elizabeth, which was granted last month. The results are pending. How the cases came about Officials have said that an investigation that started in December into sexual abuse involving two children led to the arrests of two South Bloomingville men. That probe eventually led to a separate investigation in March into Gary Jr. and Elizabeth Siders involving possible unlawful sexual conduct with a minor. On June 30, a search warrant was executed at the Siderses’ home, which led authorities to discover their 16 children living in squalid conditions. Gary Jr., Elizabeth, Gary Sr. and Christina Siders were all arrested the same day on preliminary child endangerment charges. A grand jury handed up indictments Aug. 21, charging Gary Jr., Elizabeth and Christina with 19 counts of child endangerment and Gary Siders Sr. with 16 counts. The same grand jury also indicted Gary Jr. and Elizabeth on the sexual battery and unlawful sexual conduct charges. Where the cases stand now Gary Siders Jr. pleaded not guilty to all charges Aug. 26. He remains in jail. His attorney declined to comment Thursday, citing a gag order. Last week, Gary Siders Sr., 73, was found not competent to stand trial, WSAZ reported. Dorian Baum, an attorney for Siders Sr., told The Associated Press after the hearing that the finding was not surprising. Baum said Siders’ mental health has been declining for years and is “not restorable.” “He doesn’t fully understand or appreciate what’s going on,” Baum said. Christina Siders, 68, pleaded not guilty to the initial charges and awaits arraignment on the indictment. She is in jail and is due back in court for a bond hearing Monday. NBC News has reached out to her attorney for comment. Both Gary Siders Jr. and Christina Siders also requested mental competency evaluations; the results are pending. If you are a child being abused, or know a child who may be facing abuse, call the Childhelp National Child Abuse Hotline at (800) 422-4453, or go to States often have child abuse hotlines, but if you suspect a child’s life is in imminent danger, call 911.

articles.title: Nusrat Osman: British woman rescued in deadly Malawi shootout
articles.summary: The mother of two young children was kidnapped last week in the middle of the day in the main city, Blantyre.
articles.body:
A British woman who was kidnapped in Malawi nearly a week ago has been rescued in a police operation that left four suspected kidnappers dead and a senior police chief wounded.

Nusrat Osman, 47, was freed on Thursday during an operation on the outskirts of the southern city of Blantyre, police said.

Officers exchanged gunfire with the suspected kidnappers, who police said were armed with an AK-47 rifle and a pistol.

"The criminals got shot and were rushed to the hospital where they succumbed to the injuries," the Malawi Police Service said in a statement.

Deputy Inspector General of Police Noel Kayira, who was involved in the operation, also sustained gunshot injuries and is being treated in hospital. The police statement said he was in a stable condition.

Osman was reunited with her family following the rescue and was also taken to hospital for treatment, and for physical and mental health assessments, local media reported.

Osman's younger brother, Shobi Jiwa, praised the Malawian police for securing her release, telling the UK's Sun newspaper that the family was deeply grateful for the force's efforts in investigating the kidnapping.

He also paid tribute to Kayira, the police chief who was shot during the rescue operation, describing him as the family's "hero" for putting his own life at risk to save her.

Police have not identified the four suspected kidnappers who were killed and have not provided further details about how officers located the group.

Police said she had been driving home when the men blocked her vehicle, forced her into another car and drove away.

Her disappearance prompted a major search operation, with authorities offering a reward of 30 million Malawian kwacha ($17,000; £12,500) for information leading to her rescue and the arrest and conviction of those responsible.

Osman, who is from Leicester in the UK, has lived in Malawi for several years and works for an auditing firm. She is married and has two young children.

The UK Foreign Office earlier told the BBC that it was aware of reports that a British national had been abducted in Malawi and was in touch with local authorities.

The case had puzzled investigators because police said there had been no known ransom demand or communication from the kidnappers following her disappearance.

Her family had made emotional public appeals for her safe return, describing the disappearance as deeply distressing and urging anyone with information to contact police.

The kidnapping also caused concern among Malawi's business community and British nationals living in the southern African country, where abductions of foreign nationals are relatively uncommon.

Police have not disclosed a possible motive or said whether they believe other people were involved.

They said investigations were continuing to establish the full circumstances surrounding the kidnapping and the subsequent rescue operation.

Authorities have urged the public to remain calm while the investigation continues.

articles.title: San Miguel Island had 450 foxes before golden eagles cut the population to 15; conservation efforts helped rebuild it to 322 by 2024
articles.summary: US News: In the late 1990s, San Miguel Island off the coast of Southern California was home to just 15 island foxes, down from an estimated 450. Three decades .
articles.body: In the late 1990s, San Miguel Island off the coast of Southern California was home to just 15 island foxes, down from an estimated 450. Three decades later, the population has recovered to roughly 322 animals. The turnaround followed an intensive conservation programme that tackled several causes of the decline at once, including the removal of golden eagles, the eradication of feral pigs that had helped sustain them, the reintroduction of bald eagles and a captive-breeding programme for the foxes. The collapse was not limited to San Miguel. On neighbouring Santa Rosa Island, the fox population fell from about 1,780 to 15, while Santa Cruz Island dropped from more than 1,400 to 55. In 2016, the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service removed the San Miguel, Santa Rosa and Santa Cruz Island fox subspecies from the federal endangered species list, describing the recovery as the fastest successful recovery of an Endangered Species Act-listed mammal in the United States.Why golden eagles nearly wiped out the island foxThe collapse of the northern Channel Islands' foxes was linked to a major change in the islands' predator community. Bald eagles had historically occupied the islands, but their populations declined because of DDT contamination, along with hunting and egg collection. With the bald eagles largely gone, golden eagles began establishing themselves as resident breeders on the northern Channel Islands. Unlike bald eagles, golden eagles hunt terrestrial mammals and were capable of killing the much smaller island foxes. The arrival of golden eagles coincided with the beginning of the fox decline on San Miguel. National Park Service biologists tracking 15 radio-collared foxes between 1998 and 1999 believed five had been killed by golden eagles. On Santa Cruz Island, an earlier investigation identified golden eagle predation as the cause of death for 21 of 29 fox carcasses examined.The predators also had an unusually reliable food source on the islands. Feral pigs, introduced to Santa Cruz Island in the 19th century, had multiplied into thousands of animals. Their piglets provided golden eagles with a substantial prey base, helping the large raptors establish and maintain territories on the island. The presence of this non-native food source, combined with the loss of bald eagles, helped create conditions in which golden eagles could remain on the islands and prey on foxes. San Miguel and Santa Rosa each reached just 15 foxes, while Santa Cruz fell to fewer than 80. On Santa Catalina Island, a separate threat caused a similarly dramatic decline when canine distemper killed around 90% of the fox population in the late 1990s.How removing eagles and breeding foxes reversed the declineWildlife managers recognised that simply breeding more foxes would not solve the problem while golden eagles remained on the islands. Beginning in 1999, the National Park Service and its partners started capturing and relocating golden eagles from the northern Channel Islands to the mainland. Between November 1999 and July 2006, 44 golden eagles were removed from Santa Rosa and Santa Cruz islands and released in northeastern California. Monitoring found no subsequent breeding by golden eagles on the northern Channel Islands. Managers also worked to restore the ecological conditions that had existed before the golden eagle invasion. Between 2002 and 2006, the Institute for Wildlife Studies released 61 bald eagles on Santa Cruz Island. The species eventually began nesting successfully on the northern Channel Islands, restoring a predator that could compete territorially with golden eagles without posing the same threat to island foxes.The feral pig population on Santa Cruz Island was tackled at the same time. More than 5,000 pigs were removed in 2005 and 2006, eliminating the major non-native prey source that had helped support resident golden eagles. The last feral pig was removed from Santa Cruz in 2007. Foxes were also brought into captivity as an insurance policy against extinction. Captive breeding programmes were established on the affected islands, and 226 foxes were eventually released back into the wild across the recovery effort. Captive and wild foxes were also vaccinated against canine distemper. The interventions worked together rather than operating as a single solution: predator pressure was reduced, the food source supporting golden eagles was removed and the fox populations were supplemented with captive-bred animals.From 15 foxes to roughly 322 on San MiguelThe response produced a rapid increase in fox numbers. By 2011, the San Miguel population had already returned to close to 400 adult foxes, which the National Park Service considered biologically recovered. By 2015, the island was estimated to have approximately 700 foxes. The federal government formally recognised the recovery in 2016. The U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service removed the San Miguel, Santa Rosa and Santa Cruz island fox subspecies from the endangered species list, while the Santa Catalina subspecies was downlisted from endangered to threatened. The Interior Department described the three delistings as the fastest successful recovery of an ESA-listed mammal in the United States. More recent monitoring shows that San Miguel's population has settled at a considerably lower level than the peak recorded during the recovery. According to the Island Fox Status Update 2025, compiled by Friends of the Island Fox from a May 2025 working group meeting, San Miguel had 322 foxes in 2024, down from about 525 the previous year. Researchers reported that pup numbers were typical and individual health appeared good, while the island's resources were thought capable of supporting approximately 300 to 450 foxes.The change therefore does not necessarily represent a return to the crisis conditions of the late 1990s. Instead, the latest monitoring suggests the San Miguel population may be fluctuating around the level its available resources can sustain. The island's foxes remain subject to regular monitoring because a population confined to a single island can still be vulnerable to disease, changes in food availability and renewed predator pressure. The wider Channel Islands picture also shows why continued monitoring matters. Santa Cruz Island had an estimated 3,086 foxes in 2024, while the San Clemente Island fox population recorded a third consecutive year of decline. Adult survival on San Clemente fell from an estimated 89% to 69%, and only seven pups were documented in 2024. Investigations are continuing into the causes, including possible effects from disease, food resources, wildfire and vehicle strikes. San Miguel's recovery therefore was not simply a matter of releasing captive-bred foxes into the wild. It required changing the conditions that had pushed the animals towards extinction in the first place. From 15 foxes in 1999 to roughly 322 in 2024, the population now occupies an island where the golden eagle threat has been largely removed and the ecosystem has been altered to make long-term survival possible.Catch the latest World News and Live updates.
